title: Probe a link without trusting the next frame

blocks.text: Operations want a command-line check for a new acquirer link: connect a channel, send one echo, and print `UP`, `NO_ANSWER` or `LINK_DOWN`. The first version reported `UP` on a night when the host was answering nothing, and on a busy afternoon it sat for twenty minutes before it printed anything.

Write the probe in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/EchoProbe.java`: the two methods marked `TODO`. `check` gets a connected channel, a STAN, and a time budget measured by the `clock` it was given. It must report within the budget what became of that one echo:

items: `NO_ANSWER`: the host is connected but this echo got no answer;

blocks.text: About 13 lines in total. The tests use a channel with no socket that plays a script: the host's messages, silences and hang-ups, each at a set moment on the clock.

cases.says: an echo the host answers reports the link up
a message the host sends on its own is not the answer, even when it arrives first and carries the probe's STAN
an answer is the probe's only when it carries the probe's STAN, so a late answer to an earlier echo does not count
the read timeout measures silence, so a host that keeps talking needs a deadline of the probe's own
receive() never returns null: silence ends in SocketTimeoutException, which means no answer
a closed connection ends in EOFException, which is a link down rather than a missing answer

origin.section: 3.3 `receive()` Returns the Next Frame, Not Your Answer

concepts: receive() returns the next frame, not your answer, never returns null, and its read timeout measures silence; silence and a closed connection are different exceptions.
